verses.zh: 流便子孙和迦得子孙的牲畜极其众多；他们看见雅谢地和基列地是可牧放牲畜之地，
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Now the Reubenites and the Gadites possessed a very large number of cattle. When they saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were ideal for cattle,[NOTE:2]
notes: While the tribes are on the other side of Jordan, the matter of which tribes would settle there has to be discussed. This chapter begins the settlement of Israel into the tribal territories, something to be continued in Joshua. The chapter has the petitions (vv. 1-5), the response by Moses (vv. 6-15), the proposal (vv. 16-27), and the conclusion of the matter (vv. 28-42). For literature on this subject, both critical and conservative, see S. E. Loewenstein, “The Relation of the Settlement of Gad and Reuben in Numbers 32:1-38, Its Background and Its Composition,” Tarbiz 42 (1972): 12-26; J. Mauchline, “Gilead and Gilgal, Some Reflections on the Israelite Occupation of Palestine,” VT 6 (1956): 19-33; and A. Bergmann, “The Israelite Tribe of Half-Manasseh,” JPOS 16 (1936): 224-54.
Heb “the place was a place of/for cattle.”
verses.commentary:
32:1 There are two tribes listed here that had many livestock. It is not stated if this is related to

- the capture of Midian livestock listed in Numbers 31

- livestock from Egypt (cf. Exod. 112:38)

A third tribe (i.e., half tribe) is also mentioned as desiring to dwell on this eastern side of Jordan
(i.e., Manasseh) in Num. 32:33.

These three tribes will be given the land of (Num. 32:33; Numbers 21)

- Sihon, king of the Amorites

- Og, king of Bashan

This is also found in Deut. 3:12-20 and Josh. 13:8-32; 22:1-9.

verses.zh: 就来见摩西和祭司以利亚撒，并会众的首领，说：
verses.en: the Gadites and the Reubenites came and addressed Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community. They said,
verses.commentary:
32:2 Notice the levels of leadership.

- Moses, the main leader

- Eleazar, the priest

- the leaders of the tribes (cf. Num. 32:28)

- Joshua, the soon to be successor of Moses (Num. 32:28)

verses.zh: 「亚大录、底本、雅谢、宁拉、希实本、以利亚利、示班、尼波、比稳，
verses.en: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam,[NOTE:1] Nebo, and Beon,[NOTE:2]
notes: Smr and the LXX have Sibmah. Cf. v. 38.
Cf. Baal Meon in v. 38.

verses.zh: 就是耶和华在以色列会众前面所攻取之地，是可牧放牲畜之地，你仆人也有牲畜」；
verses.en: the land that the Lord subdued[NOTE:1] before the community of Israel, is ideal for cattle, and your servants have cattle.”
notes: The verb is the Hiphil perfect of נָכָה (nakhah), a term that can mean “smite, strike, attack, destroy.”
verses.commentary: 32:4-15 This is Moses' assumption of the motives of these tribes and his warning (also v. 23).

verses.zh: 又说：「我们若在你眼前蒙恩，求你把这地给我们为业，不要领我们过约旦河。」
verses.en: So they said, “If we have found favor in your sight,[NOTE:1] let this land be given to your servants for our inheritance. Do not have us cross[NOTE:2] the Jordan River.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “eyes.”

The verb is the Hiphil jussive from עָבַר (ʿavar, “to cross over”). The idea of “cause to cross” or “make us cross” might be too harsh, but “take across” with the rest of the nation is what they are trying to avoid.
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
32:5 "If we have found favor in your sight" This is a Hebrew idiom used over 40 times in the OT. It denotes a
request from an inferior to a superior (usually YHWH, but here, Moses). This is a tactful request (two IMPERFECTS
used in a JUSSIVE sense). However, the second one made Moses think they did not want to go into Canaan at all.

verses.zh: 摩西对迦得子孙和流便子孙说：「难道你们的弟兄去打仗，你们竟坐在这里吗？
verses.en: Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, “Must your brothers go to war while you[NOTE:1] remain here?
notes: The vav (ו) is a vav disjunctive prefixed to the pronoun; it fits best here as a circumstantial clause, “while you stay here.”
verses.commentary:
32:6-15 At first Moses was not pleased. He assumed these tribes did not want to participate in the conquest of
Canaan. He also assumed this reluctance was related to the unbelief of Numbers 13 (i.e., the report of the spies).

verses.zh: 你们为何使以色列人灰心丧胆、不过去进入耶和华所赐给他们的那地呢？
verses.en: Why do you frustrate the intent[NOTE:1] of the Israelites to cross over into the land that the Lord has given them?
notes: Heb “heart.” So also in v. 9.

verses.zh: 我先前从加低斯・巴尼亚打发你们先祖去窥探那地，他们也是这样行。
verses.en: Your fathers did the same thing when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.

verses.zh: 他们上以实各谷，去窥探那地回来的时候，使以色列人灰心丧胆，不进入耶和华所赐给他们的地。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they went up to the Eshcol Valley and saw the land, they frustrated the intent of the Israelites so that they did not enter[NOTE:2] the land that the Lord had given[NOTE:3] them.
notes: The preterite with vav (ו) consecutive is here subordinated to the parallel yet chronologically later verb in the next clause.
The infinitive construct here with ל (lamed) is functioning as a result clause.
The Lord had not given it yet, but was going to give it. Hence, the perfect should be classified as a perfect of resolve.

verses.zh: 当日，耶和华的怒气发作，就起誓说：
verses.en: So the anger of the Lord was kindled that day, and he swore,

verses.zh: 『凡从埃及上来、二十岁以外的人断不得看见我对亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓应许之地，因为他们没有专心跟从我。
verses.en: ‘Because they have not followed me wholeheartedly,[NOTE:1] not[NOTE:2] one of the men twenty years old and upward[NOTE:3] who came from Egypt will see the land that I swore to give[NOTE:4] to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
notes: The clause is difficult; it means essentially that “they have not made full [their coming] after” the Lord.

The sentence begins with “if they see….” This is the normal way for Hebrew to express a negative oath—“they will by no means see….” The sentence is elliptical; it is saying something like “[May God do so to me] if they see,” meaning they won’t see. Of course here God is taking the oath, which is an anthropomorphic act. He does not need to take an oath, and certainly could not swear by anyone greater, but it communicates to people his resolve.
The LXX adds “those knowing bad and good.”
The words “to give” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
32:11 YHWH's anger at the unbelief of the Israelites in refusing to have faith in His promises to the Patriarchs
(see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS) was the death of that entire generation (i.e.,
20 years of age and up) in the wilderness (v. 13). None of them, except Joshua and Caleb, would enter Canaan (v. 12).

verses.zh: 惟有基尼洗族耶孚尼的儿子迦勒和嫩的儿子约书亚可以看见，因为他们专心跟从我。』
verses.en: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua son of Nun, for they followed the Lord wholeheartedly.’

verses.zh: 耶和华的怒气向以色列人发作，使他们在旷野飘流四十年，等到在耶和华眼前行恶的那一代人都消灭了。
verses.en: So the Lord’s anger was kindled against the Israelites, and he made them wander in the wilderness for 40 years, until all that generation that had done wickedly before[NOTE:1] the Lord was finished.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
The verb is difficult to translate, since it has the idea of “complete, finish” (תָּמָם, tamam). It could be translated “consumed” in this passage (so KJV, ASV); NASB “was destroyed.”

verses.zh: 谁知，你们起来接续先祖，增添罪人的数目，使耶和华向以色列大发烈怒。
verses.en: Now look, you are standing in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinners, to increase still further the fierce wrath of the Lord against the Israelites.
verses.commentary:
32:14

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"a brood of sinful men"

NRSV
"a brood of sinners"

TEV
"a new generation of sinful people"

NJB
"an offshoot of sinful stock"

REB
"a fresh brood of sinful men"

LXX
"a band of sinful persons"

Peshitta
"a generation of sinful people"

The MT has "a brood of sinful men." The word "brood" (BDB 916) appears only here in the OT. The
same concept of a generation or groups of sinful people is used by Jesus of the religious leaders of His day (cf. Matt. 3:7;
12:34; 23:33). Here, Moses initially accuses the tribes of Reuben and Gad of following the same path of unfaithfulness as
the Israelites in Numbers 13.

▣

NASB, JB
"to add still more"

NKJV
"to increase still more"

NRSV, NJB
"increase"

JPSOA, LXX
"add still further"

REB
"to fire"

Peshitta
"to augment still"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 705, KB 763, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), which means "sweep away," but the versions are assuming a different root
(BDB 414), meaning "to increase." The NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 278, #3, suggests that the MT root could denote "fanning or
heaping up" Israel's sin, so as to increase YHWH's fiery anger (BDB 354 CONSTRUCT BDB 60 I).

verses.zh: 你们若退后不跟从他，他还要把以色列人撇在旷野，便是你们使这众民灭亡。」
verses.en: For if you turn away from following him, he will once again abandon[NOTE:1] them in the wilderness, and you will be the reason for their destruction.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The construction uses a verbal hendiadys with the verb “to add” serving to modify the main verb.
Heb “and you will destroy all this people.”

verses.zh: 两支派的人挨近摩西，说：「我们要在这里为牲畜垒圈，为妇人孩子造城。
verses.en: Then they came very close to him and said, “We will build sheep folds here for our flocks and cities for our families,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “our little ones.”
verses.commentary:
32:16-19 The tribes of Reuben and Gad explain their intentions.

- building temporary pens for their livestock

- fortifying a few key cities for their families

- their commitment to accompanying the rest of the tribes into the conquest of Canaan

- every able bodied man would go and not return until the conquest was completed

verses.zh: 我们自己要带兵器行在以色列人的前头，好把他们领到他们的地方；但我们的妇人孩子，因这地居民的缘故，要住在坚固的城内。
verses.en: but we will maintain ourselves in armed readiness[NOTE:1] and go before the Israelites until whenever we have brought them to their place. Our descendants will be living in fortified towns as a protection against[NOTE:2] the inhabitants of the land.
notes: The MT has חֻשִׁים (khushim); the verbal root is חוּשׁ (khush, “to make haste” or “hurry”). But in light of the Greek and Latin Vulgate the Hebrew should probably be emended to חֲמֻשִׁים (hamushim), a qal passive participle meaning “in battle array.” See further BDB 301 s.v. I חוּשׁ, BDB 332 s.v. חֲמֻשִׁים; HALOT 300 s.v. I חושׁ, חישׁ; HALOT 331 s.v. I חמשׁ.
Heb “from before.”
verses.commentary:
32:17 This implies these two tribes will be the vanguard of the Israeli troops. They would not just accompany
Israel but go before them (i.e., Josh. 4:12-13, the traditional marching order of Judah).

There is an emendation suggested by the LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate. The MT has the Qal
PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, "make hast" (BDB 301, KB 300) but the ancient versions have changed it to a similar
Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, "in battle array" (BDB 332, cf. Exod. 13:18; Josh. 1:14; 4:12; Jdgs. 1:11;
NEB, NJB).

verses.zh: 我们不回家，直等到以色列人各承受自己的产业。
verses.en: We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has his inheritance.

verses.zh: 我们不和他们在约旦河那边一带之地同受产业，因为我们的产业是坐落在约旦河东边这里。」
verses.en: For we will not accept any inheritance on the other side of the Jordan River[NOTE:1] and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this eastern side of the Jordan.”
notes: The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 摩西对他们说：「你们若这样行，在耶和华面前带着兵器出去打仗，
verses.en: Then Moses replied,[NOTE:1] “If you will do this thing, and if you will arm yourselves for battle before the Lord,
notes: Heb “said to them.”
verses.commentary: 32:20-27 Moses was pleased with their suggestion and promise.

verses.zh: 所有带兵器的人都要在耶和华面前过约旦河，等他赶出他的仇敌，
verses.en: and if all your armed men cross the Jordan before the Lord until he drives out his enemies from his presence
verses.commentary:
32:21 "you armed men" The VERB (BDB 323, KB 321, Niphal IMPERFECT,
cf. Num. 32:17, 20, 30; 31:3; Josh. 6:7, 9, 13), basically means "to strip," but in this military context, it means to equip oneself for
battle (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 157-158).

verses.zh: 那地被耶和华制伏了，然后你们可以回来，向耶和华和以色列才为无罪，这地也必在耶和华面前归你们为业。
verses.en: and the land is subdued before the Lord, then afterward you may return and be free of your obligation to the Lord and to Israel. This land will then be your possession in the Lord’s sight.
verses.commentary:
32:22 "be free of obligation toward the Lord" This ADJECTIVE
(BDB 667) denotes freedom from a vow/oath (cf. Josh. 2:17, 20). Although this context does not mention an oath, it is surely implied.

verses.zh: 倘若你们不这样行，就得罪耶和华，要知道你们的罪必追上你们。
verses.en: “But if you do not do this, then look, you will have sinned[NOTE:1] against the Lord. And know that your sin will find you out.
notes: The nuance of the perfect tense here has to be the future perfect.

verses.zh: 如今你们口中所出的，只管去行，为你们的妇人孩子造城，为你们的羊群垒圈。」
verses.en: So build cities for your descendants and pens for your sheep, but do what you have said[NOTE:1] you would do.”
notes: Heb “that which goes out/has gone out of your mouth.”

verses.zh: 迦得子孙和流便子孙对摩西说：「仆人要照我主所吩咐的去行。
verses.en: So the Gadites and the Reubenites replied to Moses, “Your servants will do as our lord[NOTE:1] commands.
notes: Heb “my lord” (also v.27)

verses.zh: 我们的妻子、孩子、羊群，和所有的牲畜都要留在基列的各城。
verses.en: Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our livestock will be there in the cities of Gilead,

verses.zh: 但你的仆人，凡带兵器的，都要照我主所说的话，在耶和华面前过去打仗。」
verses.en: but your servants will cross over, every man armed for war, to do battle in the Lord’s presence, just as our lord says.”

verses.zh: 于是，摩西为他们嘱咐祭司以利亚撒和嫩的儿子约书亚，并以色列众支派的族长，说：
verses.en: So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the families of the Israelite tribes.
verses.commentary: 32:28-32 Moses states clearly the conditions and consequences of the two tribes' promises.

verses.zh: 「迦得子孙和流便子孙，凡带兵器在耶和华面前去打仗的，若与你们一同过约旦河，那地被你们制伏了，你们就要把基列地给他们为业。
verses.en: Moses said to them: “If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, each one equipped for battle in the Lord’s presence, and you conquer the land,[NOTE:1] then you must allot them the territory of Gilead as their possession.
notes: Heb “and the land is subdued before you.”

verses.zh: 倘若他们不带兵器和你们一同过去，就要在迦南地你们中间得产业。」
verses.en: But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must receive possessions among you in Canaan.”

verses.zh: 迦得子孙和流便子孙回答说：「耶和华怎样吩咐仆人，仆人就怎样行。
verses.en: Then the Gadites and the Reubenites answered, “Your servants will do what the Lord has spoken.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “that which the Lord has spoken to your servants, thus we will do.”

verses.zh: 我们要带兵器，在耶和华面前过去，进入迦南地，只是约旦河这边、我们所得为业之地仍归我们。」
verses.en: We will cross armed in the Lord’s presence into the land of Canaan, and then the possession of our inheritance that we inherit will be ours on this side of the Jordan River.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 摩西将亚摩利王西宏的国和巴珊王噩的国，连那地和周围的城邑，都给了迦得子孙和流便子孙，并约瑟的儿子玛拿西半个支派。
verses.en: So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and to half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the realm of King Sihon of the Amorites, and the realm of King Og of Bashan, the entire land with its cities and the territory surrounding them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the land with its cities in the borders of the cities of the land all around.”
verses.commentary: 32:33 Without explanation half of the tribe of Manasseh chooses to be a part of this compact.

verses.zh: 迦得子孙建造底本、亚他录、亚罗珥、
verses.en: The Gadites rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

verses.zh: 亚他录・朔反、雅谢、约比哈、
verses.en: Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,

verses.zh: 伯・宁拉、伯・哈兰，都是坚固城。他们又垒羊圈。
verses.en: Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran as fortified cities, and constructed pens for their flocks.

verses.zh: 流便子孙建造希实本、以利亚利、基列亭、
verses.en: The Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,

verses.zh: 尼波、巴力・免、西比玛（尼波、巴力・免，名字是改了的），又给他们所建造的城另起别名。
verses.en: Nebo, Baal Meon (with a change of name), and Sibmah. They renamed[NOTE:1] the cities they built.
notes: Heb “called names.”
verses.commentary:
32:38 The pagan cities of "Nebo" and "Baal-meon" had their names changed by the Israelites but the text does
not mention the new names.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did Reuben and Gad want to settle on the eastern side of the Jordan?

- How did Reuben and Gad get so much more livestock than their brothers?

- Why was Moses initially so angry with them?

- What did Reuben and Gad

- ask of Moses?

- promise to do?

verses.zh: 玛拿西的儿子玛吉，他的子孙往基列去，占了那地，赶出那里的亚摩利人。
verses.en: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, took it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were in it.

verses.zh: 摩西将基列赐给玛拿西的儿子玛吉，他子孙就住在那里。
verses.en: So Moses gave Gilead to Machir, son of Manasseh, and he lived there.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in it.”

verses.zh: 玛拿西的子孙睚珥去占了基列的村庄，就称这些村庄为哈倭特・睚珥。
verses.en: Now Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their small towns and named them Havvoth Jair.[NOTE:1]
notes: Havvoth Jair. The Hebrew name means “villages of Jair.”

verses.zh: 挪巴去占了基纳和基纳的乡村，就按自己的名称基纳为挪巴。
verses.en: Then Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name.

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations

Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 32:1-5

1Now the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad had an exceedingly large number of livestock. So when they
saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, that it was indeed a place suitable for livestock, 2the sons of Gad
and the sons of Reuben came and spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation, saying,
3"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon, 4the land which the
Lord conquered before the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants
have livestock." 5They said, "If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants as a
possession; do not take us across the Jordan."
